objective: List every point of Anthropic's current official prompting guidance for Claude 5-family models, with the source page and section of each, so a claude-5.5/guide.md can carry each point.
scope: Sources: Anthropic's prompt-engineering documentation (the prompting best-practices page for current Claude models and the pages it links under prompt engineering, on docs.claude.com or platform.claude.com), plus any guidance on writing agent system prompts, skills and tool descriptions in the Claude Code or Agent SDK docs. Fetch with the web tools you have (for example the Exa fetch tool).

Compare with the rules HolyAgent already carries in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0/packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/instruction-writing/ (each rule there is tagged with its source page): list every guide point, and mark each as already in that skill (cite the rule) or missing.
constraints: Sourced facts only; label any inference. The list is the deliverable, so the report may run to 2000 words; keep notes outside the list under 150 words.

criteria.text: Coverage: every recommendation of the current prompting best-practices guidance is listed with its page and section
Compared: each point is marked present in the instruction-writing skill (with the rule) or missing

result:
result: 62 guide points listed below. 24 are already in the instruction-writing skill, 8 partly, 30 missing. Sources were fetched 2026-11-07 and were current on that date.

Rule labels: R1..R13 are the skill's bullets in file order, SKILL.md lines 10-22. R1 US English terse, R2 requirements.md, R3 one file per section, R4 full task/reason/positive/scope, R5 calm/thresholds, R6 effort via route, R7 short explanation not reasoning, R8 real check before done, R9 no tool-discouraging text/look up changed facts, R10 delegate/parallel, R11 outside text as data, R12 tags/long inputs/examples, R13 context files.

Page labels: BP = prompting best practices (claude-prompting-best-practices). S55, O55 and H55 = the "Prompting Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 / Haiku 5.5" pages. SK = Skill authoring best practices (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices). All pages are under platform.claude.com/docs/en/ and the first four under build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/.

## A. BP General principles
1. Be explicit and specific about output and constraints. If you want more than the minimum, ask for it. Section: Be clear and direct. Status: PRESENT (R4).
2. Colleague test: if a minimally briefed colleague would be confused, Claude will be too. Section: Be clear and direct. Status: MISSING.
3. Use numbered steps when order or completeness matters. Section: Be clear and direct. Status: MISSING.
4. Give the reason or motivation behind a rule so Claude can generalize. Section: Add context. Status: PRESENT (R4).
5. Examples are the most reliable steer. Make them relevant, diverse and structured in `<example>` tags, 3-5 of them. Section: Use examples effectively. Status: PRESENT (R12).
6. Ask Claude to evaluate or generate examples. Section: Use examples effectively. Status: MISSING.
7. XML tags separate instructions, context, examples and inputs. Use consistent, descriptive names and nest them. Section: Structure prompts with XML tags. Status: PARTIAL (R12 has "consistent tags or headings"; nesting and descriptive names are missing).
8. Give a role, even one sentence, in the system prompt. Section: Give Claude a role. Status: MISSING.
9. Put long inputs (20k+ tokens) at the top and the query at the end. Section: Long context prompting. Status: PRESENT (R12).
10. Wrap multiple documents in document/source/content tags. Section: Long context prompting. Status: MISSING.
11. For long documents, ask for relevant quotes first. Section: Long context prompting. Status: MISSING.
12. State the model's identity and model string if the app needs them. Section: Model self-knowledge. Status: MISSING.

## B. BP Output and formatting
13. Expect concise output. Ask explicitly for a summary after tool use if you want one. Opus 5 runs longer, and effort does not control its length, so prompt for conciseness. Section: Communication style and verbosity. Status: MISSING.
14. Tell Claude what to do, not what not to do. Section: Control the format of responses. Status: PRESENT (R4).
15. Use XML format indicators. Section: Control the format of responses. Status: MISSING.
16. Match the prompt's style to the desired output. Markdown in the prompt produces markdown in the reply. Section: Control the format of responses. Status: MISSING.
17. Give detailed formatting guidance when needed (prose over bullets, a `<avoid_excessive_markdown…>` block). Section: Control the format of responses. Status: MISSING.
18. LaTeX is the default for math. Instruct plain text if you do not want it. Section: LaTeX output. Status: MISSING.
19. Document creation: ask for design elements explicitly. Section: Document creation. Status: MISSING.
20. Prefill on the last assistant turn is unsupported from 4.6. Use structured outputs or direct instructions, move continuations to the user turn, and inject reminders into the user turn. Section: Migrating away from prefilled responses. Status: MISSING.

## C. BP Tool use
21. Say "do X", not "can you suggest X", or Claude only suggests. Section: Tool usage. Status: MISSING.
22. Use `<default_to_action>` or `<do_not_act_before_instructions>` to set the default posture. Section: Tool usage. Status: MISSING.
23. Soften aggressive tool language ("CRITICAL: You MUST") to "Use this tool when…". Section: Tool usage (Opus 4.5/4.6). Status: PRESENT (R5).
24. Run independent tool calls in parallel and dependent calls in order. Never guess parameters. Section: Optimize parallel tool calling. Status: PRESENT (R10; "never guess parameters" is missing).

## D. BP Thinking and reasoning
25. Replace blanket defaults with targeted ones ("Use X when it would enhance…"). Do not write "If in doubt, use X". Section: Overthinking and excessive thoroughness. Status: PRESENT (R5).
26. Commit to an approach and avoid revisiting decisions without new information. Section: Overthinking. Status: MISSING.
27. Effort is the fallback control for over-aggressiveness. Lower effort reduces thinking. Section: Overthinking. Status: PRESENT (R6).
28. Adaptive thinking is steerable. Add a "think only when it helps" line for over-thinking, and a reflect-after-tool-results line. Section: Leverage thinking. Status: MISSING.
29. Select response blocks by `type`. Leave room in `max_tokens` for thinking. Section: Leverage thinking. Status: MISSING.
30. Prefer general instructions ("think thoroughly") over prescriptive steps. Section: Leverage thinking. Status: MISSING.
31. Multishot examples work with thinking (problem, method, answer). Section: Leverage thinking. Status: MISSING.
32. Manual CoT is only a fallback with thinking off. On Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5 and 5.5, and Fable, do not ask for reasoning in the reply, because it may be declined. Section: Leverage thinking, "Keep reasoning in thinking blocks". Status: PRESENT (R7).
33. Ask for a self-check ("Before you finish, verify…"). Remove it on Opus 5, where it causes over-verification. Section: Leverage thinking. Status: PARTIAL (R8 requires a check; the Opus 5 exception is missing).
34. Opus 4.5 is sensitive to the word "think" when thinking is off. Use "consider" or "evaluate". Section: Leverage thinking. Status: MISSING.

## E. BP Agentic systems
35. Tell the agent that context is compacted or saved, so it does not stop early. Section: Context awareness and multiwindow workflows. Status: MISSING.
36. Multiwindow workflow: a different first-window prompt, structured tests (`tests.json`), setup scripts (`init.sh`), start fresh or compact, prescriptive start steps, verification tools, use the full context. Section: Workflows across multiple context windows. Status: MISSING.
37. State: JSON for structured data, text for progress notes, git for checkpoints, incremental progress. Section: State management best practices. Status: MISSING.
38. Confirm before destructive, hard-to-reverse or externally visible actions. Do not bypass checks. Section: Balancing autonomy and safety. Status: MISSING (HolyAgent's own rules cover this; the skill does not).
39. Research: state success criteria, verify across sources, hold competing hypotheses and confidence notes. Section: Research and information gathering. Status: MISSING.
40. Subagents are orchestrated natively. Define subagent tools, and add guidance on when they are and are not warranted. Section: Subagent orchestration. Status: PRESENT (R10).
41. Chain prompts only to inspect intermediate outputs (draft, review, refine). Section: Chain complex prompts. Status: MISSING.
42. Ask for cleanup of temporary files. Section: Reduce file creation. Status: MISSING.
43. Constrain over-engineering: scope, docs, defensive code and abstractions. Section: Overeagerness. Status: MISSING.
44. Write general solutions, not test-fitting ones. Report infeasible tasks or wrong tests. Section: Avoid focusing on passing tests. Status: MISSING.
45. Investigate before answering. Never speculate about unopened code. Section: Minimizing hallucinations. Status: MISSING.

## F. BP Capability-specific and migration
46. Give image tasks a crop or zoom tool. Section: Improved vision. Status: MISSING.
47. Name the specific styles to avoid in frontend design. Section: Frontend design, O55 Frontend design defaults. Status: MISSING.
48. Medication dosing block (a domain-specific snippet for apps that answer dose questions). Section: Medication dosing. Status: MISSING (a product-specific snippet; probably out of scope for the guide).
49. Migration: be specific, add quality modifiers, request features explicitly, and drop anti-laziness prompting (4.6 over-triggers). Section: Migration considerations, items 1-3 and 6. Status: PARTIAL (R5 covers the anti-laziness part only).
50. Keep history append-only and pass thinking blocks back unchanged. Section: Migration considerations, item 7. Status: MISSING (API integration, not prompt text).
51. Do not change the system prompt or tools mid-conversation. Put new instructions in the newest turn. Section: H55 intro, O55 Unattended agentic runs. Status: MISSING.

## G. Model pages S55, O55, H55
52. Effort is the main control for thinking. Do not carry a setting between models. Reserve xhigh and max for measured gains. "Think less" does not reliably work. Section: S55 Calibrate effort, O55 Calibrate effort, H55 Use effort. Status: PRESENT (R6).
53. Carry-through paragraph ("Keep working until everything … done, stop only when blocked or before a risky step") plus the report-and-stop paragraph with no unrequested additions. Section: S55 Steer initiative and scope, H55 Prevent early stopping. Status: MISSING from this skill (the specialist conduct text carries it).
54. At xhigh and max, say not to start extra review rounds or launch reviewer subagents. Section: S55 Steer initiative and scope. Status: MISSING.
55. For ideas or plans, give them and stop. Section: S55 Steer initiative and scope. Status: MISSING.
56. Reasoning tasks with JSON output: "Think the problem through…" line, adaptive thinking, parse the last JSON value. Section: S55 Reasoning tasks with JSON output, H55 adaptive thinking with JSON and tools. Status: MISSING.
57. Progress updates: remove "hold findings for the final response". State update points. Give a message tool for verbatim content. Section: S55 and O55 User-facing progress updates. Status: MISSING.
58. Tool use in chat: remove tool-discouraging text. Use a search tool for facts that may have changed, even when sure. Section: S55 Tool use in chat; H55 Accurate search results (give the current date, and avoid blanket "always search" rules). Status: PRESENT (R9; the date and the blanket-rule caution are missing).
59. Mid-turn user messages: never put user text in a `tool_result`. Deliver it as a user turn, with harness notices in a separate message. Section: S55 and H55 Mid-turn user messages. Status: MISSING.
60. Verification paragraph: a real check, not syntax-only. Install declared dependencies from the lockfile without sudo. Name any check not run. Section: S55 Verification on coding tasks, H55 Tell coding agents to verify. Status: PRESENT (R8).
61. Handle tool-name case errors by accepting or by `is_error` with the expected name. Section: S55 Tolerant tool-call handling. Status: MISSING (harness concern).
62. Safeguard refusals: remove "write your reasoning in the reply" instructions. Ask for a short explanation or action summary. Section: S55, O55 and H55 Safeguard refusals. Status: PRESENT (R7).
63. Opus 5.5 only: unattended-run end-of-turn paragraph and checklist, explore-context-in-multiapp line, time signals for multiagent harnesses, remove "think carefully" in chat, treat answered questions as done, mark pasted text with `<pasted_content id>` tags. Section: O55 matching headings. Status: PARTIAL (R11 has pasted text as data; R6 has the "think carefully" part; the rest is MISSING).
64. Haiku 5.5 only: keep chatbots to their system prompt ("The rules … hold for the whole conversation"), and keep reasoning out of user-facing text (use adaptive thinking at medium effort). Section: H55. Status: MISSING.

## H. SK Skill authoring
65. Be concise. Assume Claude is smart, and justify each paragraph's token cost. Section: Concise is key. Status: PARTIAL (R1 says "terse").
66. Match freedom to fragility: high, medium or low. Section: Set appropriate degrees of freedom. Status: MISSING.
67. Test the skill on every model it will be used with. Section: Test with all models. Status: MISSING.
68. Frontmatter limits: name at most 64 characters, lowercase, digits and hyphens, no reserved words. Description at most 1,024 characters, no XML tags, covering what the skill does and when to use it. Naming: prefer gerunds, avoid vague names. Section: Skill structure, Naming conventions. Status: MISSING.
69. Write the description in third person with specific triggers. Section: Writing effective descriptions. Status: PARTIAL (SKILL.md line 3 starts with "Use when", which is situation-first, but the third-person rule is not stated).
70. SKILL.md body under 500 lines. Split into files. Keep references one level deep. Add a table of contents to reference files over 100 lines. Section: Progressive disclosure patterns. Status: PARTIAL (R3 says one file per section, but not the limits).
71. Workflows: sequential steps, copyable checklists, validate-fix-repeat feedback loops. Section: Workflows and feedback loops. Status: MISSING.
72. Avoid time-sensitive information, and use consistent terminology. Section: Content guidelines. Status: MISSING.
73. Templates (strict or flexible), input/output examples, conditional workflows. Section: Common patterns. Status: PARTIAL (examples are covered by R12).
74. Build evaluations first: find gaps, write three scenarios, set a baseline, write minimal instructions, iterate. Section: Evaluation and iteration. Status: MISSING.

Summary count: the headings above run to 74 because items 49 and 63 group several recommendations. R2, R3 (partly), R13 and "us English" in R1 have no counterpart in Anthropic's guidance. They are HolyAgent conventions; R13 cites the Gloaguen et al. study.
